messages:
alex.k: Quick proposal — build a small orchestrator called `prime-scheduler` that unifies deploy-time warmers, autoscale-triggered primes, and nightly scheduled priming. Keep it lightweight and observable.

mira: curious what you mean by "unifies" — one service that decides when to send synthetic requests, or a framework for exporters to plug in?

alex.k: One service + small runner libs. The scheduler owns policies (on-deploy, on-scale-up, scheduled windows) and emits events. Runners (k8s job / lambda / dedicated process) translate events into synthetic traffic.

sam: +1. needs careful rate controls tho. Last time we ran synthetic bursts we hit token quota and spiked infra.

jordan: we also need to think about cache keying. If warmers use slightly different truncation/whitespace, hit rate drops. We should standardize the keying function.

alex.k: Agreed — propose using the production prefix-key normalization utilities (exact same normalization path used by runtime): strip trailing spaces, normalize unicode NFKC, collapse multiple spaces, truncate to 1024 chars, then hash with farmhash64. Will document exact algorithm.

mira: can we add a quick snippet that runner uses to generate warmup requests? Example:

```
# warmup runner (pseudo)
for p in prefixes_to_prime:
  body = normalize_prefix(p)
  curl -s -X POST https://redwood-infer.internal/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $WARMER_KEY' -d "{\"input\": \"${body}\", \"max_tokens\": 1}"
```

sam: love having the exact curl. Also need a header to mark requests as synthetic so we can filter telemetry (X-Primed-By: prime-scheduler).

jordan: telemetry: please start with these time-series: cache.prefix.hits, cache.prefix.misses, cache.prefix.hitrate (per-prefix quantiles), runtime.latency.p50/p95 during warmup windows, and model.qps.

nora: how do we prevent warmers from regressing CPU/GPU perf? If we send many short requests we could degrade batch size distribution and cause worse latency for real traffic.

alex.k: Good point. Plan: runners will emulate production inter-arrival patterns and preferred sequence lengths. We will cap synthetic qps per shard and prefer to run during low-traffic windows or on spare capacity nodes. Also add an adaptive throttle: if runtime.latency.p95 spikes > 1.5x baseline, pause.

mira: we should have two priming modes: "prefix-only" (send short prompts to populate KV cache) and "session-warm" (simulate multi-token sessions to warm kernel paths and kv updates). The latter will use a low concurrency, longer sequences.

sam: any thoughts about warmers on autoscale events? We often scale up 50–100% and come up cold. Triggering warmers from the HPA event seems useful but racy.

jordan: trigger rule: when scaler transitions from N to N+M with M>=2 or when new node group joins, schedule a progressive prime: 10% immediate, then linear ramp over 5 minutes. Keep per-node limits.

nora: important to attach idempotency tokens so repeated primes for same node/pool don't overcount. Also record node_id + prime_run_id in telemetry.

alex.k: PERF data: ran a small test last week — naive burst warmers gave prefix hit-rate increases from 8% -> 62% for the targeted prefixes, but P95 latency on prod traffic increased 12% during peak. With capped qps + adaptive pause, hit-rate still reached 45% with negligible latency impact.

mira: can you paste the test summary?

alex.k: pasted below: 

```
Test: deploy-prime-v1
Targets: 250 hot prefixes (customer app flows)
Naive burst: qps=500 for 30s -> prefix_hitrate: 8% -> 62%
  side-effect: runtime.p95 +12% (baseline 110ms -> 123ms)
Capped adaptive: qps=120 steady + ramp -> prefix_hitrate: 45%
  side-effect: runtime.p95 +1.5% (110ms -> 111.7ms)
Cost: extra tokens ~0.02% of daily token usage
```

sam: that's encouraging. Key follow-ups: billing-safe warmers (don't bill customers), and safety circuit that stops if model GPU utilization > 80%.

jordan: regarding cache key collisions — we should maintain a small sample of (prefix_hash -> raw_prefix) in S3 for debug. Also compute per-prefix hit-rate decay over time (half-life) to decide prime cadence.

mira: rollout plan idea: start in staging with 2 runner pods, test with staging prefixes, then dark-launch to 10% of production traffic (no user-facing changes), compare prefix.hitrate lift and p95 delta for 24 hours, then ramp 25/50/100.

nora: add ops playbook: how to abort a run, rollback button in console, and an alert if synthetic-run causes error rates > 0.5% or p95 > baseline*1.25.

alex.k: I'll draft an RFC with the scheduler API (events: ON_DEPLOY, ON_SCALE_UP, SCHEDULE_WINDOW, MANUAL), runner spec, normalization code, and telemetry dashboard wireframes.

mira: one more ask — privacy: warmers should avoid real user data. Use curated synthetic prefixes derived from anonymized histograms or developer-provided canonical prefixes. No customer PII in warmers.

sam: thanks — I'll work on runner rate-limiter + quota enforcement.

jordan: I'll add a telemetry dashboard prototype and the per-prefix decay heuristic.

nora: ops will write the abort/playbook and console controls.

deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: prime-scheduler RFC draft -> review board on Mon 09:00. :calendar: 

alex.k: Thanks everyone — I'll post the RFC link here once it's up.
